LESSON: A scope that is a data structure needs its authorisation ON the entry. Putting the ruling in a sibling comment or a doc means widening the scope is an edit; requiring every listed county to be NAMED IN THE ENTRY'S OWN RULING makes widening a sentence someone has to be willing to write. The guard costs four lines at module load and was observed failing in both directions in one sitting -- adding a county without the sentence refuses to import.

A gate that must skip something should return the skip as DATA (rail, scope, ruling, and the skipped thing's own verdict) rather than as an absence. The same field is then the drift detector: if a skipped rail ever carries 'pass', the record says so, and the two systems that disagree have somewhere to be seen disagreeing.

Two instruments can hold the same fact and disagree (AF-1). The publish gate asks 'is this rail on this county's floor'; the exit ledger asks 'does this rail read excluded'. P-292 answers the first correctly and, by leaving the verdict honest, makes the second read INCOMPLETE. When a lane's correct change makes another instrument wrong, the wrongness is part of the deliverable -- report it with line numbers instead of routing around it.

Round-Tripping a guard is cheaper than arguing about it: three minutes of scratch edits turned 'the map cannot be widened without a test failing' from a claim into 19/19 -> 12/7 evidence, and the revert is the proof the tree is clean.

When a dispatch's falsifier and the dispatch's own mission item disagree, pre-register the narrower bound AND the declared exception in CP1. Falsifier 3 said 'the gate module and tests only'; mission item 3 required a publish record that names the skip; the 4-line field in another file is what reconciles them, and saying so before the code existed is what keeps it from reading as scope creep.
DEAD-END: Writing `not-applicable` cells for maxImperviousCoverPct outside Travis. It would fabricate an absence -- Austin's watershed rules govern its jurisdiction in Williamson and Hays (13,924 and 411 austin-tx parcels in P-255's census) and acquire-edwards-recharge-zone feeds the rail from a cross-county aquifer zone. The honest state outside Travis is 'not acquired', i.e. unaccounted.
Removing the rail from PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS for everyone, or making the floor county-specific at the SLATE level: it would drop a real Travis requirement, and the dispatch forbids it.

Changing `checked` to mean the county's floor. test/publish.test.mjs:2182 pins checked against DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS.length and PR #157 is rewriting that same test; a second PR touching it would collide by construction.
